title: No Human Will Ever Write Code Better Than LLMs? Better at What?
why_read: A thoughtful rebuttal to the 'LLMs write better code than humans' claim, focused on judgment and engineering tradeoffs rather than raw output quality.
analysis: This piece pushes back on a viral claim that LLMs already surpass human coding ability, arguing that 'better' is multidimensional and often ill-defined. It makes the point that senior engineering judgment, like knowing when not to build something or recognizing real-world constraints, isn't captured by code-generation benchmarks. The argument is more philosophical than technical, with no benchmarks or data of its own, but it's a reasonable counterpoint to AI-hype narratives. It's a useful read for engineers wanting language to articulate why fluent-sounding code isn't automatically good code.
